PROJECT: PEACHTREE CORNERS LOAN & PAWN

Premium Website Redesign — Frontend Demonstration

You are an expert senior web developer, UI/UX designer, brand strategist, conversion optimization specialist, and technical SEO engineer.

Your assignment is to independently design and build a polished, premium, modern website prototype for:

Business: Peachtree Corners Loan & Pawn
Location: 7040 Jimmy Carter Boulevard, Suite 4, Peachtree Corners, GA 30092
Phone: 678-691-1692
Existing website: https://pawnshopnorcross.com

This project is being developed as a professional website demonstration for the business owners. It is intended to demonstrate the quality of a possible replacement website and the value of ongoing website, marketing, and technology support.

This is a FRONTEND PROTOTYPE FIRST.

Do not connect to, modify, replace, or interfere with the existing website, domain, hosting, business accounts, or live systems.

---

1. YOUR AUTONOMY AND RESPONSIBILITY

You have permission to make independent technical and design decisions.

Choose the technology stack you believe is best suited to this project.

Evaluate the available environment, existing dependencies, and project structure before making changes.

You may choose React, Next.js, Vite, Tailwind CSS, or another suitable modern frontend architecture.

Prioritize:

- Excellent visual quality.
- Responsive design.
- Maintainable code.
- Fast loading.
- Accessibility.
- Search-engine-friendly structure.
- Reusable components.
- Easy future expansion.

Do not ask me to choose frameworks, libraries, fonts, component systems, or implementation details unless absolutely necessary.

Do not stop at a design proposal, wireframe, or implementation plan.

Build the working website.

If something is unavailable, make a reasonable decision and continue.

---

2. BRAND DIRECTION AND VISUAL IDENTITY

Create a luxury retail aesthetic using a sophisticated black-and-gold visual identity.

The website should feel like a premium jewelry and specialty retail business, not a generic pawn shop template.

Color palette

Use a carefully balanced palette:

- Deep black: #090909
- Charcoal: #171717
- Warm gold: #C5A15A
- Champagne gold: #E2C58A
- Soft ivory: #F6F2E9
- Muted gray: #A7A7A7

Gold should be used strategically for accents, buttons, borders, icons, highlights, and typography.

Avoid excessive gold backgrounds.

Typography

Use a sophisticated editorial serif font for major headings and a clean modern sans-serif font for body text and navigation.

Suggested combinations:

- Playfair Display + Inter
- Cormorant Garamond + Manrope
- DM Serif Display + DM Sans

Choose the combination that creates the strongest visual identity.

Design characteristics

- Elegant spacing.
- Large editorial headlines.
- High-quality product photography.
- Subtle transitions and hover effects.
- Refined borders and separators.
- Strong visual hierarchy.
- Premium product cards.
- Consistent alignment.
- Carefully controlled shadows.
- Beautiful mobile navigation.

The result should look custom-designed rather than generated from a generic template.

Avoid:

- Cheap-looking gold gradients.
- Excessive animations.
- Cluttered layouts.
- Cartoon-style icons.
- Generic stock-template sections.
- Oversized rounded cards everywhere.
- Unnecessary visual effects.

---

3. WEBSITE ARCHITECTURE

Build a multi-page frontend experience with the following pages.

PAGE 1: HOME

Create a visually impressive homepage that immediately establishes the brand.

Navigation

Include:

- Logo / business name.
- Home.
- Shop.
- Jewelry.
- Electronics.
- Tools.
- Musical Instruments.
- Sell to Us.
- Pawn Loans.
- About.
- Contact.

Use a refined responsive navigation system.

Include a prominent gold-accented call-to-action button.

Hero section

Create a large editorial hero section.

Suggested headline:

VALUE WORTH DISCOVERING.

Supporting text:

"Explore quality jewelry, electronics, tools, musical instruments, and unique finds at Peachtree Corners Loan & Pawn."

Primary CTA: Explore Merchandise

Secondary CTA: Visit Our Store

Use premium retail imagery featuring jewelry, watches, electronics, or carefully arranged specialty merchandise.

Do not use imagery that misrepresents the actual business inventory.

Featured categories

Create visually attractive category sections for:

1. Jewelry & Watches
2. Electronics
3. Tools & Equipment
4. Musical Instruments
5. Collectibles & Specialty Finds

Each category should have an image, title, short description, and clickable destination.

Featured merchandise

Build a beautiful product showcase with demonstration products.

Use realistic placeholder products, but clearly identify them as demonstration inventory.

Suggested examples:

- Gold-tone or fine jewelry pieces.
- Luxury-style watches.
- Wireless headphones.
- Professional power tools.
- Musical equipment.

Do not represent demonstration products as verified items currently available at the store.

Do not invent actual inventory, prices, brands, or availability.

Why visit us?

Create a section focused on:

- Discovering unique merchandise.
- Exploring changing inventory.
- Getting assistance from the store team.
- Visiting the Peachtree Corners location.

Do not invent customer testimonials, awards, years in business, or business achievements.

Store visit section

Display the business address and phone number.

Include:

- Call the Store button.
- Get Directions button.
- Store information.

Do not publish unverified opening hours.

---

PAGE 2: SHOP

Create a dedicated merchandise browsing experience.

Features:

- Product category filters.
- Search field.
- Product cards.
- Product images.
- Product names.
- Demonstration inventory labels.
- View Details actions.

Use local demonstration data stored in the frontend.

Products should be organized into categories.

Create reusable components so actual merchandise can be added later.

Do not implement checkout, payment processing, purchasing, or live inventory synchronization.

---

PAGE 3: JEWELRY

Create a premium jewelry landing page.

Feature:

- Jewelry editorial photography.
- Watches.
- Rings.
- Necklaces.
- Bracelets.
- Jewelry category browsing.
- Contact-the-store CTA.

Make this page feel especially luxurious.

Do not make unsupported claims about precious-metal purity, authenticity, certifications, or product availability.

---

PAGE 4: ELECTRONICS

Create a clean electronics browsing page.

Categories may include:

- Phones.
- Computers.
- Audio equipment.
- Gaming.
- TVs and accessories.
- Other electronics.

Use demonstration products only.

Include a notice that availability changes and visitors should contact the store to verify current inventory.

---

PAGE 5: TOOLS & EQUIPMENT

Create a dedicated page for:

- Power tools.
- Hand tools.
- Workshop equipment.
- Outdoor equipment.
- Specialty tools.

Use strong product photography and simple category navigation.

---

PAGE 6: MUSICAL INSTRUMENTS

Create a visually engaging page featuring:

- Guitars.
- Keyboards.
- Audio equipment.
- Recording equipment.
- Musical accessories.

Use editorial-style photography.

---

PAGE 7: SELL TO US

Create a page explaining that visitors can contact the store about merchandise they may wish to sell.

Suggested headline:

TURN WHAT YOU OWN INTO AN OPPORTUNITY.

Explain that customers should contact the store directly to discuss items and applicable requirements.

Create a frontend inquiry form containing:

- Name.
- Email.
- Phone.
- Item category.
- Item description.
- Optional estimated value.
- Message.

Clearly label the form as a demonstration.

Do not collect sensitive personal information, government identification, financial information, passwords, or customer account details.

The form must not pretend to submit information to the actual business.

Implement frontend validation and a clear demonstration success state.

---

PAGE 8: PAWN LOANS

Create an informational page introducing the possibility of contacting the business about pawn services.

Use careful, neutral wording.

Suggested headline:

QUESTIONS ABOUT PAWN SERVICES?

Encourage visitors to contact the store directly to discuss applicable terms, eligibility, documentation, and requirements.

Do not invent:

- Interest rates.
- Loan amounts.
- Loan terms.
- Fees.
- Eligibility requirements.
- Redemption periods.
- Legal disclosures.
- Approval guarantees.

Do not create an online loan application or collect financial information.

The page should be informative without making unsupported financial or legal claims.

---

PAGE 9: ABOUT

Create an elegant business introduction page.

Use only verified business information.

Do not invent:

- Founding date.
- Ownership history.
- Years of operation.
- Employee biographies.
- Awards.
- Community partnerships.
- Customer statistics.

Use general, honest language about the shopping experience and the types of merchandise visitors may explore.

Include a store visit CTA.

---

PAGE 10: CONTACT

Create a polished contact page.

Include:

Business name: Peachtree Corners Loan & Pawn

Address:
7040 Jimmy Carter Boulevard, Suite 4
Peachtree Corners, GA 30092

Phone:
678-691-1692

Include:

- Click-to-call phone link.
- Directions link.
- Contact inquiry form.
- Map section or map placeholder.
- Clear contact information.

Use the following directions destination:

https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=7040+Jimmy+Carter+Boulevard+Suite+4+Peachtree+Corners+GA+30092

Do not invent operating hours.

---

4. FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS

This must be a functioning frontend prototype, not a static mockup.

Implement:

- Working navigation.
- Responsive mobile menu.
- Reusable header and footer.
- Functional category navigation.
- Product category filtering.
- Product search.
- Product detail views or modals.
- Working phone links.
- Working directions link.
- Frontend inquiry form validation.
- Demonstration success messages.
- Clear demonstration inventory labels.
- Responsive layouts.
- Accessible buttons and form labels.
- Keyboard-accessible interactions.

All buttons must have meaningful behavior.

Do not create buttons that look functional but do nothing.

For features that require a backend, implement a clear frontend demonstration state instead.

---

5. TECHNICAL IMPLEMENTATION

Organize the project cleanly.

Use reusable components wherever practical.

Suggested component structure:

- Header
- Footer
- Navigation
- HeroSection
- CategoryCard
- ProductCard
- ProductGrid
- ProductFilters
- ProductSearch
- ContactSection
- InquiryForm
- StoreInformation
- CallToAction
- PageLayout

Use a centralized data structure for demonstration products and categories.

Keep business contact information in one centralized configuration file so it can be updated easily.

Use local assets or appropriate image sources.

Do not hotlink questionable copyrighted product photography or use images that falsely imply specific inventory.

Use descriptive image alt text.

Ensure:

- No broken image links.
- No console errors.
- No missing routes.
- No broken navigation.
- No horizontal overflow on mobile.
- No unnecessary dependencies.
- No exposed API keys or secrets.

---

6. SEARCH ENGINE OPTIMIZATION

Implement foundational SEO.

Include:

- Unique page titles.
- Unique meta descriptions.
- Semantic HTML.
- Logical heading hierarchy.
- Descriptive image alt attributes.
- Clean URL structure.
- Internal links.
- Open Graph metadata.
- Appropriate canonical handling for the demo environment.

Use natural local search language where appropriate, including:

- Peachtree Corners pawn shop.
- Pawn shop near Norcross.
- Jewelry in Peachtree Corners.
- Electronics and tools.
- Pawn services.

Do not claim guaranteed search rankings.

Do not create fake reviews, fake ratings, fake business listings, or misleading structured data.

Do not add fabricated operating hours or unsupported business details to structured data.

---

7. DEMONSTRATION AND BUSINESS PROTECTION

This website is an independent demonstration.

Important restrictions:

- Do not change the existing website.
- Do not connect to the actual domain.
- Do not modify DNS.
- Do not modify hosting.
- Do not connect Google Business Profile.
- Do not connect Facebook or Instagram.
- Do not connect payment processors.
- Do not connect customer databases.
- Do not create real customer records.
- Do not send messages to customers.
- Do not collect or store real customer information.

Clearly distinguish demonstration content from verified business information.

Create a small, tasteful demonstration notice where appropriate.

Do not make the entire website look like an unfinished demo. It should look like a professional production-quality design while remaining technically isolated.

---

8. QUALITY ASSURANCE

After implementation, thoroughly test the website.

Check:

1. Every page loads.
2. Every navigation link works.
3. Mobile navigation works.
4. Product filtering works.
5. Product search works.
6. Product details open correctly.
7. Inquiry form validation works.
8. Demonstration success states work.
9. Phone link opens correctly.
10. Directions link opens correctly.
11. Images load correctly.
12. No horizontal overflow.
13. No major accessibility problems.
14. No console errors.
15. No broken routes.

Run the available build and lint commands.

Resolve errors instead of simply reporting them.

Do not stop until the prototype is usable and visually polished.

---

9. FINAL DELIVERABLES

When finished, provide:

1. A working local website preview.
2. The complete source code.
3. A concise explanation of the chosen technology stack.
4. A list of completed pages.
5. A list of functional features.
6. A list of anything still using demonstration data.
7. Instructions for running the project.
8. A list of what would be needed to move from prototype to production.

Also identify the highest-value next improvements that could be added after the owners review the demonstration.

---

10. YOUR FINAL OBJECTIVE

Think like a professional digital agency delivering a premium website concept to a real business owner.

The result should make the owners immediately understand:

- Their business could have a stronger online presence.
- Customers could browse merchandise more easily.
- The store could present its products more professionally.
- The website could make contacting and visiting the business easier.
- The design can be expanded into a real business platform later.

Do not build something that looks like a school project.

Build something that looks like a premium retail brand invested in its digital presence.

Start by inspecting the project environment, choose the appropriate technology stack, and then implement the complete frontend prototype.

A polished, modern website redesign prototype has been designed and built for **Peachtree Corners Loan & Pawn**.

### 🔗 Live Prototype Preview
**[Open Peachtree Corners Loan & Pawn Website Demonstration](https://antigravity.luch.dev/site/9f7c8288-36d4-48c5-9376-a200e0c955d0/61828e2cf85fa5093de0d99b/)**  
*(Saved automatically and viewable directly in your browser)*

---

### 1. Technology Stack & Design Rationale

| Layer | Technology | Rationale |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Framework** | **React 18** | High-performance component-driven architecture for rapid browsing, instant category switching, and interactive modals. |
| **Styling** | **Tailwind CSS** | Custom-configured luxury black-and-gold design system (`#090909` obsidian, `#171717` charcoal, `#C5A15A` warm gold, `#E2C58A` champagne gold, and `#F6F2E9` ivory). |
| **Typography** | **Cormorant Garamond + Plus Jakarta Sans** | Editorial luxury serif for headlines combined with a clean geometric sans-serif for optimal readability and modern prestige. |
| **Iconography** | **Lucide React** | Clean, minimalist, scalable vector icons with zero visual clutter. |
| **Routing** | **Dual Path & Hash Router** | Static-hosting compatible SPA routing supporting bookmarking, instant URL updates, and zero 404 page reloads. |
| **Build Tool** | **Vite** | Sub-second hot-reloading and lightweight production bundle. |

---

### 2. Completed Pages & Architecture

All 10 requested pages have been built and styled:

1. **Home (`/`)**:
   - Editorial hero section with the headline: **"VALUE WORTH DISCOVERING."**
   - High-impact visual retail showcase with primary CTA (*Explore Merchandise*) and secondary CTA (*Visit Our Store*).
   - Department highlights for Jewelry & Watches, Electronics, Tools, Instruments, and Collectibles.
   - Featured demonstration merchandise showcase with quick-view modal triggers.
   - **"Why Visit Peachtree Corners Loan & Pawn?"** value pillars (unique merchandise, changing inventory, dedicated team, accessible location).
   - Store visit section with verified address, direct phone link, and directions CTA.
2. **Shop (`/shop`)**:
   - Complete merchandise catalog browsing experience.
   - Live real-time search field (filtering by title, subcategory, and description).
   - Department filter pills (All, Jewelry & Watches, Electronics, Tools, Instruments, Collectibles).
   - Sort dropdown (*Featured*, *Price: Low to High*, *Price: High to Low*, *Name: A to Z*).
   - Interactive product cards with demonstration badges and "View Details" quick view.
3. **Jewelry (`/jewelry`)**:
   - Luxury landing page featuring watches, rings, necklaces, and bracelets.
   - Department filters for fine watches, diamond solitaires, gold chains, and tennis bracelets.
   - In-person gold and diamond evaluation information explaining certified testing standards.
4. **Electronics (`/electronics`)**:
   - Tech browsing for laptops, smartphones, noise-canceling headphones, and gaming consoles.
   - 3-step testing protocol highlight (data wipe, port/hardware inspection, hands-on in-store testing).
   - Availability notice advising visitors to call ahead.
5. **Tools & Equipment (`/tools`)**:
   - Commercial-grade cordless combo kits, miter saws, rotary lasers, and compressors.
   - Contractor equipment guidance and tools trade-in consultation.
6. **Musical Instruments (`/musical-instruments`)**:
   - Guitars (electric and acoustic), tube combo amplifiers, and weighted stage pianos.
   - Musician-friendly details on action setup and sound testing.
7. **Sell to Us (`/sell-to-us`)**:
   - Headline: **"TURN WHAT YOU OWN INTO AN OPPORTUNITY."**
   - Transparent 4-step selling process (gather items, bring valid photo ID, in-person evaluation, immediate payout).
   - Detailed breakdown of evaluated merchandise categories.
   - Interactive, validated frontend inquiry form with demonstration success state.
8. **Pawn Loans (`/pawn-loans`)**:
   - Headline: **"QUESTIONS ABOUT PAWN SERVICES?"**
   - Neutral, respectful, legally compliant collateral overview.
   - Clear "What to Bring" checklist (photo ID, physical item, accessories).
   - Clear disclosure that terms are handled in person per Georgia regulations.
9. **About (`/about`)**:
   - Introduces Peachtree Corners Loan & Pawn's retail vision and commitment to an elevated customer experience.
   - Verified location at 7040 Jimmy Carter Blvd in Peachtree Corners / Norcross.
10. **Contact (`/contact`)**:
    - Complete business information, click-to-call link, and Google Directions link.
    - Operating hours notice advising visitors to call ahead.
    - Validated contact inquiry form.
    - Embedded interactive map centering on 7040 Jimmy Carter Blvd.

---

### 3. Key Functional Features

- **Quick-View Product Details Modal**: Clicking "View Details" on any product opens an overlay with specifications, condition badges, estimated value, direct telephone link, and an online inquiry action.
- **Frontend Inquiry Validation**: The inquiry forms validate name, email, phone number, category, and description before presenting a demonstration confirmation receipt.
- **Responsive Mobile Navigation**: A sleek slide-out drawer menu featuring quick action buttons (*Call Store*, *Get Directions*) and categorized department links.
- **Centralized Business Configuration**: Business details (address, phone, map coordinates, legal disclaimers) are centralized in [`src/data/storeInfo.js`](file:///home/agent/workspace/src/data/storeInfo.js).
- **Centralized Catalog Data**: Demonstration items and categories are organized in [`src/data/inventory.js`](file:///home/agent/workspace/src/data/inventory.js).

---

### 4. Demonstration Data Notice

To protect the business and maintain technical isolation:
- **Demonstration Inventory**: Product photos, specifications, and values are realistic representations.
- **Demonstration Forms**: Form submissions validate inputs on the frontend and display a confirmation dialog; no customer data is transmitted to live databases.
- **Store Hours**: Opening hours are intentionally omitted with a polite notice inviting visitors to call `(678) 691-1692` for daily schedules.

---

### 5. Moving From Prototype to Production

When the store owners are ready to transition this into a live digital asset, the recommended roadmap includes:
1. **Live Inventory Integration**: Connect a lightweight Headless CMS or POS export (e.g., Bravo Pawn Systems or PawnMaster) to display verified in-store stock in real time.
2. **Form Backend & SMS Notifications**: Connect inquiries to the store’s official email or SMS notification line for rapid appraisal responses.
3. **Verified Operating Hours & Google Business Profile Sync**: Add official operating hours and embed Google Reviews via Google Business Profile API.
4. **Enhanced Local SEO**: Deploy JSON-LD structured data for `LocalBusiness` and `PawnShop` schemas.

---

*Note: If you wish to connect a GitHub repository to back up your commit history, tap the GitHub mark at the top of the chat interface.*

PROJECT: PEACHTREE CORNERS LOAN & PAWN

THE VAULT — FULL-STACK COMMERCE, INVENTORY & CUSTOMER PLATFORM

You are acting as a senior software architect, full-stack engineer, e-commerce developer, cybersecurity engineer, UI/UX designer, database architect, and marketing automation specialist.

Your task is to transform the existing Peachtree Corners Loan & Pawn website prototype into a sophisticated, secure, full-stack retail commerce platform.

This is an expansion of the existing Antigravity project.

Preserve the existing luxury black-and-gold branding and all successful frontend work. Inspect the current codebase before making changes.

Do not unnecessarily rebuild working components.

BUSINESS INFORMATION

Business: Peachtree Corners Loan & Pawn

Address:
7040 Jimmy Carter Boulevard, Suite 4
Peachtree Corners, GA 30092

Phone: 678-691-1692

Existing website: https://pawnshopnorcross.com

Brand identity:

- Deep black.
- Charcoal.
- Champagne gold.
- Warm gold accents.
- Premium editorial typography.
- Luxury retail photography.
- Elegant product displays.

The platform should feel like a premium retail brand with the operational capabilities of a modern e-commerce business.

1. ARCHITECTURE AND AUTONOMY

Independently select the best technology stack for this application.

Evaluate the existing project before choosing technologies.

Use a maintainable architecture that supports:

- Frontend application.
- Backend application/API.
- Secure database.
- Customer authentication.
- Administrative authentication.
- Product and inventory management.
- Order management.
- Payment processing integration.
- Email automation.
- SMS automation.
- Marketing subscriptions.
- Customer account management.

You may choose a suitable managed backend such as Supabase, Firebase, or an equivalent platform.

Use secure, server-side operations for privileged actions.

Do not store passwords in plaintext.

Do not store payment card numbers or CVV information.

Never expose secret API keys in frontend code.

Use environment variables for credentials.

Create a clear ".env.example" documenting required configuration without including actual secrets.

If credentials or external services are unavailable, build the integration adapters and a working demonstration mode.

Do not pretend that an external integration is live when it is not.

2. CUSTOMER ACCOUNT SYSTEM

Create a complete customer registration and login experience.

Customers should be able to:

- Create an account.
- Sign in.
- Sign out.
- Verify their email address.
- Reset forgotten passwords.
- Update their profile.
- Change their password.
- View their order history.
- View order details.
- View order status.
- Manage marketing preferences.
- Manage email subscriptions.
- Manage SMS subscriptions.
- Request account deletion.

Customer profile fields:

- First name.
- Last name.
- Email.
- Phone number.
- Password managed by the authentication provider.
- Account creation date.
- Marketing consent preferences.

Allow browsing without an account.

Allow guest checkout if the selected payment and order architecture supports it.

Do not force customers to create accounts to browse merchandise.

Never expose one customer's order information to another customer.

3. THE VAULT — LIVE MERCHANDISE SYSTEM

Build The Vault as the central attraction of the website.

The Vault should display:

- New arrivals.
- Recently added products.
- Featured merchandise.
- Weekly drops.
- Special promotions.
- Category collections.
- Limited-quantity merchandise.

Create a visually impressive homepage section:

THE VAULT

JUST CAME IN.

"Discover what's new before somebody else does."

Every product should support:

- Product name.
- Product description.
- Category.
- Brand, when verified.
- Product condition.
- Actual selling price.
- Quantity available.
- Product photographs.
- Date added.
- Availability status.
- Featured status.
- New-arrival status.
- Product SKU or internal identifier.

Inventory statuses:

- Draft.
- Available.
- Reserved.
- Sold.
- Archived.

Create a New Arrivals collection that updates automatically whenever authorized staff publish new merchandise.

Create a Featured Drops collection for weekly promotions.

Create a product search and category filtering system.

Allow staff to publish products immediately or schedule their publication.

Do not display products marked sold or unavailable as purchasable.

Clearly communicate when inventory changes quickly.

Never fabricate actual merchandise, prices, brands, quantities, or availability.

4. ADMINISTRATIVE DASHBOARD

Create a separate secure administration area.

Suggested route:

/admin

The dashboard should look like a professional retail management system.

Dashboard overview:

- Total active products.
- Available inventory count.
- Sold inventory count.
- New arrivals.
- Pending orders.
- Completed orders.
- Recent sales.
- Recent inventory changes.
- Customer registrations.
- Newsletter subscribers.
- Recent administrative activity.

Create an attractive black-and-gold administrative interface.

INVENTORY MANAGEMENT

Authorized administrators must be able to:

- Add products.
- Upload multiple photographs.
- Edit product descriptions.
- Edit selling prices.
- Update quantities.
- Assign categories.
- Set product conditions.
- Mark products as featured.
- Publish new arrivals.
- Schedule product releases.
- Mark products sold.
- Archive products.
- Search inventory.
- Filter by category and status.

Make product creation straightforward.

Create a dedicated Add Product interface with image upload, pricing, category selection, and publication controls.

Use image compression and appropriate storage permissions.

Maintain an inventory change history.

Record which administrator created or modified each product.

ORDER MANAGEMENT

Administrators must be able to:

- View orders.
- Search orders.
- View order details.
- View customer contact information when authorized.
- View payment status.
- View fulfillment status.
- Update order status.
- Add internal order notes.
- Process permitted cancellations and refunds through the payment provider.
- Record fulfillment and pickup information.

Order statuses:

- Pending payment.
- Paid.
- Processing.
- Ready for pickup.
- Shipped.
- Completed.
- Cancelled.
- Refunded.

Use server-side payment verification.

Never mark an order paid simply because the customer returned to a success page.

5. ADMINISTRATOR CREATION AND PERMISSIONS

Create a role-based administrative access system.

There must be an initial OWNER / SUPER ADMIN role.

The owner-level administrator must be able to:

- Create additional administrators.
- Invite administrators by email.
- Assign administrative roles.
- Change administrator permissions.
- Suspend administrator access.
- Revoke administrator access.
- Review administrative activity.

Create these roles:

OWNER / SUPER ADMIN:

- Full system access.
- Create and manage administrators.
- Manage roles and permissions.
- Manage inventory.
- Manage orders.
- Manage customers.
- Manage promotions.
- View reporting.
- Manage integrations and settings.

INVENTORY MANAGER:

- Create products.
- Edit products.
- Upload images.
- Update pricing.
- Update quantities.
- Publish and archive merchandise.
- View relevant inventory reports.

ORDER MANAGER:

- View orders.
- Update fulfillment statuses.
- Manage pickup and shipping workflows.
- Add internal notes.

MARKETING MANAGER:

- Manage promotions.
- Create Vault Drops.
- Manage approved marketing campaigns.
- Create and schedule marketing content.
- View campaign reporting.

An administrator may only create or manage users at permission levels they have explicitly been granted.

Only the OWNER / SUPER ADMIN may create another OWNER / SUPER ADMIN.

Do not allow ordinary administrators to promote themselves or bypass permission restrictions.

Use secure invitation links with expiration.

Require appropriate authentication and preferably multi-factor authentication for administrators.

Never hardcode default administrative passwords.

Create a secure first-owner bootstrap procedure using environment configuration or a protected setup process.

Record administrator creation, role changes, suspensions, deletions, inventory modifications, and other privileged operations in an audit log.

6. WEBSITE CHECKOUT AND PURCHASE SYSTEM

Create a complete online shopping experience.

Customers must be able to:

- Browse merchandise.
- View product details.
- Add available items to their cart.
- Change quantities where inventory permits.
- Remove items.
- Review their cart.
- Enter contact information.
- Choose available fulfillment options.
- Review the order.
- Complete checkout.
- Receive an order confirmation.

Support configurable fulfillment methods:

- In-store pickup.
- Shipping, if enabled by the owners.

Display applicable taxes, shipping costs, and order totals before payment.

Create order confirmation pages.

Create customer order records.

Prevent overselling.

Use atomic inventory reservations or an equivalent transaction-safe process during checkout.

Release reservations when payment fails or expires.

Handle duplicate payment notifications safely.

PAYMENT PROVIDER REQUIREMENTS

Do not assume that every payment provider permits pawn-shop businesses or every merchandise category.

Investigate provider eligibility and merchant-account approval requirements before activating payments.

Build a payment-provider abstraction so an approved provider can be connected without rewriting the application.

Possible providers may include Square, Stripe, or another provider approved for this specific business and its merchandise.

Use hosted or tokenized payment checkout.

Do not collect or store raw card details.

Do not activate real payments without explicit business-owner approval and valid provider credentials.

Initially use sandbox/test payments.

Do not process pawn loans through retail checkout.

Do not sell firearms or other regulated products through this prototype.

Exclude any merchandise category that requires additional legal, licensing, payment-provider, or shipping approval until the owners have reviewed and authorized it.

IMPORTANT: IN-STORE SALES

The business wants purchases routed through the website.

Design the architecture to support a unified sales record for website purchases and in-store purchases.

Investigate whether the existing store uses a POS system and whether it supports an approved API or inventory synchronization.

Do not claim real-time unified inventory until synchronization is implemented and tested.

If POS integration is unavailable, provide an administrative in-store sale recording workflow and clearly document its limitations.

The long-term objective is one accurate inventory system rather than separate, conflicting online and in-store stock counts.

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENT: SMART INVENTORY INTAKE — TWO-MODE PRODUCT ENTRY

This feature is a major operational priority.

The inventory system must be extremely easy for everyday retail staff to use.

The objective is to eliminate unnecessary data entry, reduce repetitive work, and make inventory publishing fast enough that staff will actually use it consistently.

Do not build a clunky administrative form with dozens of mandatory fields.

Create a polished, intuitive Smart Inventory Intake experience with TWO distinct product-entry modes.

MODE 1: MANUAL ADD

Create a traditional manual product-entry workflow for staff who want complete control.

Allow authorized staff to enter:

- Product title.
- Category.
- Brand.
- Model.
- SKU or internal identifier.
- Description.
- Product condition.
- Selling price.
- Quantity.
- Product photographs.
- Search tags.
- Featured status.
- New-arrival status.
- Publication status.

Allow multiple photographs to be uploaded, reordered, previewed, and removed.

Use logical sections and progressive disclosure.

Do not display every optional field at once.

Require only the information necessary to safely publish a product.

Save Draft and Publish should be clearly visible.

Preserve entered information if the user navigates away accidentally or experiences a temporary upload failure.

MODE 2: QUICK ADD AI

Build an intelligent photo-first product intake workflow.

This mode should be the fastest way to add ordinary merchandise.

STEP 1: PHOTO UPLOAD

Present a large, easy-to-understand upload area.

Allow staff to:

- Upload multiple images.
- Drag and drop images on supported devices.
- Take photos directly using a mobile device camera.
- Preview uploaded images.
- Reorder photographs.
- Remove unwanted photographs.

Support common image formats.

Compress large photographs appropriately without destroying product detail.

Display upload progress and useful error messages.

STEP 2: AI PRODUCT ANALYSIS

After photographs are uploaded, analyze the images using an appropriate vision-capable AI service.

Extract or suggest:

- Likely product identity.
- Category.
- Visible brand.
- Visible model information.
- Product type.
- Observable physical characteristics.
- Cosmetic condition observations.
- Suggested product title.
- Customer-friendly product description.
- Search tags.
- Suggested primary image.

Where supported, detect visible model numbers or product markings.

Do not invent information that cannot be established from the photographs.

Every generated field should have a confidence indicator or an appropriate verification status.

Examples:

- Confirmed visually.
- AI suggestion — verify.
- Not identified.
- Requires manual inspection.

Never claim that an item functions correctly based only on appearance.

Never certify precious metals, gemstones, luxury goods, electronics, or other merchandise as authentic based only on images.

Never automatically assign an exact model, serial number, purity, authenticity, or technical specification without sufficient evidence.

STEP 3: HUMAN REVIEW

Show staff a clean product review screen.

Display:

- Product photographs.
- Suggested title.
- Suggested category.
- Suggested brand.
- Suggested model.
- Suggested description.
- Suggested tags.
- Condition observations.

Allow staff to edit every suggested field.

Clearly highlight fields that need verification.

The staff member must confirm the actual selling price and quantity.

The AI must never independently decide the actual store selling price or publish a product without the required staff authorization.

STEP 4: SAVE OR PUBLISH

Provide three clear actions:

1. Save Draft.
2. Publish Product.
3. Publish and Add Another.

After a successful save, display a simple confirmation.

Allow staff to immediately start the next item without returning to the dashboard.

The system should generate the product page, product card, inventory record, and New Arrivals entry automatically where appropriate.

QUICK BATCH MODE

Support adding multiple products in one session.

Staff should be able to upload several groups of product photographs and create separate draft products.

Each group of images must be associated with the correct product.

Do not combine unrelated products into one listing.

Provide a simple batch review screen where staff can move between products, correct details, enter prices, and publish approved items.

If AI processing fails for one item, do not lose the other uploads.

Allow individual products to be retried.

MOBILE-FIRST EXPERIENCE

Design this workflow primarily for staff using an iPhone or Android phone inside the store.

Make the controls large and easy to tap.

Use a camera-first interface.

Minimize typing.

Use sensible defaults and remember non-sensitive workflow preferences.

Avoid unnecessary modal windows and multiple confirmation screens.

Make it possible to complete a typical listing with minimal interaction.

The staff member should never have to navigate through a complicated administrative dashboard just to add a product.

INVENTORY QUALITY CONTROL

Every product must have a clear status:

- Draft.
- AI analysis pending.
- Needs review.
- Ready to publish.
- Published.
- Sold.
- Archived.

Prevent publication when required verified information is missing.

Maintain an audit trail showing which administrator approved the product and when.

Never overwrite a published product with new AI-generated content without human approval.

DESIGN REQUIREMENTS

The experience must feel simple, modern, and effortless.

Prioritize:

- One-screen clarity.
- Minimal typing.
- Large upload controls.
- Visible progress.
- Fast feedback.
- Easy correction.
- Clear save and publish actions.
- Consistent visual design.
- Mobile responsiveness.

Do not make the user feel like they are completing a spreadsheet.

Avoid excessive required fields, unnecessary popups, confusing navigation, and repetitive confirmations.

The overall experience should be closer to uploading a photograph to a social media platform than entering an item into an old-fashioned inventory database.

PERFORMANCE AND RELIABILITY

Use asynchronous AI processing.

Show progress while analysis is running.

Allow users to continue working on other drafts where practical.

Implement retry handling.

Prevent duplicate products caused by accidental double submission.

Preserve image uploads and entered information if AI processing fails.

Provide a manual fallback at all times.

Use secure image storage and server-side AI requests.

Do not expose AI provider API keys in frontend code.

Clearly separate AI-generated suggestions from staff-confirmed product information.

SUCCESS CRITERION

A staff member who is not particularly technical should be able to add an ordinary product without training.

The normal Quick Add process should require:

1. Photograph the item.
2. Upload the photos.
3. Review AI-generated information.
4. Confirm price and quantity.
5. Publish.

Build this as a first-class part of the inventory system, not as an afterthought.
